main_body: A flat grass ground patch, 4x3 tiles, tiled with a repeating pattern of green with sparse light and dark speckles
top_band: none (terrain tile, no standing object; the column scan shows only speckle variation of one green)
evidence: This is a ground terrain patch, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. The column scan shows one green (L=113) with occasional 1-2 row speckles of lighter (136) and darker (91) green. There is no wall, cliff or roof structure that would need a top band and a front face. The kind matches terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 colours per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours in the reference grass. It has 3 green steps (dark, mid, light) where the reference grass has about 5 or more. Flat-fill coverage is 19% against 0% for the reference. The speckle is sparse and repeats on an exact grid (the same clump pattern recurs every 16 px), with no varied tufts, clumps or soil grain. Next to the reference grass it looks thinner and flatter, and the visible tiling is stronger.
